Evidence record
When was it measured or observed?Observations published by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) for the first three quarters of 2024 (subscribers), 2024 Q3, 2025 H1 and September 2025; later official context is kept separately.
Who or what does it apply to?Wallet/e-wallet provider counts and e-wallet subscriber counts as defined by each cited source of the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden); the provider definition, subscriber definition and counting basis may differ by source.

Wallet and subscriber counts from different publications are not yet reconciled

Report an error

01What does this evidence establish?

Official CBY-Aden publications report different wallet counts at different dates and in different contexts—7 in 2024 Q3, 9 in 2025 H1 and 8 licensed e-wallets in a September 2025 official statement. The 2024 Q3 payments report gives e-wallet subscriber counts of 414,631, 507,585 and 581,075 for the first three quarters of 2024, and the H1 2025 infographic gives 2,102,484 for 2025 H1. Because definitions and reporting scope have not been reconciled across these publications, neither set is presented as a continuous trend, and subscribers are not unique people or active users.

02What does it measure?

Counts of e-wallets and of e-wallet subscribers published by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) for dates from the first quarter of 2024 to September 2025, whose definitions have not been reconciled.

03Who or what does it apply to?

Wallet/e-wallet provider counts and e-wallet subscriber counts as defined by each cited source of the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden); the provider definition, subscriber definition and counting basis may differ by source.

04How current is it?

The latest wallet count in this record is the September 2025 statement of 8 licensed e-wallets, and the latest subscriber count is 2,102,484 for 2025 H1. A later source does not extend either series unless its definition is shown to be comparable.

05What this evidence does not establish

The sequence 7, 9 and 8 does not show providers entering or leaving the market, or net growth in providers. The move from 581,075 subscribers (2024 Q3) to 2,102,484 (2025 H1) is not a measure of growth, and subscribers are not unique people or active users. Why the numbers differ: the January 2025 baseline of active e-wallet accounts of the World Bank-financed FMIIP project (record FMIIP-BASELINE-2025-01) is far lower than the 2025 subscriber count here. The project publishes its own definition of an active e-wallet account; the CBY-Aden payments infographic for the first half of 2025 gives no definition of a subscriber. The two have not been reconciled, so the gap cannot be read as growth, as inactivity or as an error, and neither is a count of people. The same CBY-Aden infographic reports 5,202,019 accounts for the first half of 2025 — a count of accounts in its reporting scope, under no published definition, not of people. Nor can the 2024 subscriber counts here be read as a fall from the e-money accounts counted in December 2019 (record CLM-050): that study covered five providers and counted accounts, under a definition never reconciled with CBY-Aden's.

07Method and verification detail

Detail for reproducing or challenging this record without changing what it means.

How was it produced?

The counts are compared across publications of the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) by date, label, provider definition and counting basis. That comparison has not established that 7, 9 and 8 measure the same thing, or that the 2024 quarterly subscriber counts and the 2025 H1 subscriber count do.

When does this record change?

This record is updated when an authoritative source is revised or replaced, a newer comparable observation becomes available, the definition, population or method changes, or the conditions for public use change.

How can I verify it?

This record is drawn from the source(s) listed on this page. Open a source record to reach the original document, and check that the definition, period, population and geography match what is stated here.

How should this record be read?

Read this evidence within the definition, population or group covered, calculation base where relevant, period, geography and method shown on the page. Before reusing or comparing it, check the source, limitations, evidence date and correction history. If a value or source link is unavailable, the page says so rather than filling the gap by inference. This resource does not host source files; where an original-source link is given, check the publisher’s terms before republishing.
